is_transient.instructions: Given the job metadata and the last 200 log lines in state, decide whether this failure looks transient/environmental (network blip, DNS/registry timeout, runner or infra flake, disk/resource exhaustion, rate limiting) as opposed to a deterministic failure caused by the code or test changes themselves.

criteria.true: The log shows signs of an environmental/infra problem: network timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, registry/package-mirror errors, runner provisioning errors, out-of-disk/out-of-memory, container pull failures, or other issues unrelated to the actual code under test.
criteria.false: The log shows a deterministic failure: a failing assertion, a compile/type error, a lint error, a stack trace pointing into application or test code, or any failure that would reproduce identically on a clean retry.

failure_category.instructions: Classify the root cause of this CI job failure using the log tail and job metadata in state.

criteria.infra_flake: Network, DNS, package registry, container registry, or CI-runner infrastructure problem.
criteria.resource_exhaustion: Out of memory, out of disk, CPU/timeout limits, or other resource exhaustion on the runner.
criteria.flaky_test: A test failed in a way typical of flakiness (timing, ordering, race condition) rather than a real logic error.
criteria.code_defect: A real bug or regression in application/test code caused a legitimate assertion failure, compile error, or type error.
criteria.dependency_error: A specific dependency/package version conflict or missing dependency error, not a general network flake.
criteria.unknown: The log does not give enough evidence to classify the failure confidently.

retry_value.instructions: Considering the failure category, the transience signal, and how many attempts this job has already had (attempt vs max_attempts in state), estimate how valuable it is to automatically retry this job.
